moments.title: An Irish parish is founded
moments.text: Irish immigrants founded St. Patrick's parish on Easter morning, 1846.

moments.title: Cornerstone laid
moments.text: Work began on the parish's permanent church on the West Side.

moments.title: Dedicated on Christmas Day
moments.text: The new church was dedicated on Christmas Day, 1856.

moments.title: Spared by the Great Fire
moments.text: The fire passed about two blocks from the church, which came through untouched. Because it survived, it is often called the oldest public building in the city.

moments.title: The first block party
moments.text: The parish's first "World's Largest Block Party" drew about 5,000 people to Desplaines St, according to the church.

moments.title: On the National Register
moments.text: Old St. Patrick's was listed on the National Register of Historic Places. One source says it was also among the first buildings named a Chicago Landmark, in 1964.

moments.title: Today: Old St. Pat's
moments.text: The church at 700 W. Adams St is still an active parish, and its summer block party is still held.

sources.title: Architecture in Chicago: Surviving Structures (University of Illinois Library)

checked.notes: Parish founded 1846; cornerstone May 23, 1853; dedicated Christmas Day 1856; fire missed it by about two blocks; first block party 1956 (Old St. Patrick's history page, Clio).
